Expert visceral angiography is the investigation of choice in patients with obscure gastrointestinal haemorrhage.

the most common lesion causing obscure gastrointestinal bleeding is angiodysplastic lesions of the colon, and that the most important investigation for obscure gastrointestinal bleeding is visceral angiography.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in 131 patients with obscure gastrointestinal bleeding, 69 were shown to have a lesion by visceral angiography, 23 at laparotomy and 11 at endoscopy; 21 had no lesion.

in the presence of melaena, the first investigation should be a barium meal, the second a barium enema, and the third a barium meal with small bowel follow-through; in the presence of rectal bleeding, the first investigation is sigmoidoscopy, the second colonoscopy and the third barium enema.

in 131 patients with obscure gastrointestinal bleeding, colonic angiodyplasia was responsible for haemorrahage in 52 patients, small bowel vascular anomalies in 16 patients, Meckel's in nine patients, small bowel smooth muscle neoplasms in seven patients, and gastric vascular lesions in four patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

80 per cent of patients over 45 with obscure gastrointestinal bleeding can be cured by angiographic localization and selective embolization, whereas 60 per cent of patients under 45 can be cured by laparotomy.
the majority of patients (60%) with obscure gastrointestinal bleeding have a benign lesion which can be treated by endoscopic or surgical techniques.

the investigation and management of 'obscure gastrointestinal bleeding' is best undertaken by a team of surgeons, radiologists and gastroenterologists with a common interest in the subject, and that the management of these patients should be individualised to suit their particular needs.

the majority of patients with obscure GI bleeding have an underlying cause, and that a careful and methodical approach to the investigation of these patients is essential to ensure a successful outcome.
